questions.question: How many positive factors of 444 are there?
questions.solution:
444 = 2² × 3 × 37

Hence, number of positive factors = 3 × 2 × 2 = 12 

∴ The number of positive factors of 444 = 12

**Alternate Method:**

(1 x 444) (2 x 222) (3 x 148) (4 x 111) (6 x 74) (12 x 37) (37 x 12) (74 x 6) (111 x 4) (148 x 3) (222 x 2) (444 x 1)

List of all Positive Factors of 444 in numerical order:

1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, 37, 74, 111, 148, 222, and 444.

∴ The number of positive factors of 444 = 12

questions.question: What will be the remainder when (631 × 632 × 633) is divided by 5?
questions.solution:
Units digit of (631 × 632 × 633) = 1 × 2 × 3 = 6

⇒ Remainder when 6 is divided by 5 = 1

∴ The remainder when (631 × 632 × 633) is divided by 5 = 1

questions.question: What is the least number added to 700, so that number becomes multiple of 17?
questions.solution:
Remainder of (700 ÷ 17) is 3.

⇒ Nearest multiple of 17 = 700 – 3 = 697

Next multiple of 17 = 697 + 17 = 714 = 700 + 14

∴ The least number to be added to 17 so that it’s a multiple of 17 = 14

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 30 days. He worked for 6 days and B finished the remaining work in 48 days. B alone can do the whole work in how many days?
questions.solution:
Work done by A in one day = 1/30

Work done by A in 6 days = 6/30 = 1/5

Remaining work = 1 – (1/5) = 4/5

∴ Time taken by B alone to do the whole work = 48/(4/5) = 60 days

questions.question: Three taps A, B and C can fill an tank in 50, 60 and 75 hours respectively. How long (in hours) would the three taps take to fill the tank if all of them are opened together?
questions.solution:
Work done by tap A in one hour = 1/50

Work done by tap B in one hour = 1/60

Work done by tap C in one hour = 1/75

Work done if all the three taps are opened together = (1/50) + (1/60) + (1/75) = (6 + 5 + 4)/300 = 15/300 = 1/20

∴ Time taken to fill the tank if all of them are opened together = 1/(1/20) = 20 hours

questions.question: The lengths of two diagonals of a rhombus are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the side (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
We know that,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3644aed2619f5dc50c5063f4d5c624f8b575276857e4c751dfee963227c98902.png] 

Side of a rhombus with diagonals** d₁ **and** d₂ = √(d₁² + d₂²)/2**

⇒ Side of the rhombus = √(8² + 6²)/2 = √100/2 = 10/2 = 5 cm

∴ Side of the rhombus = 5 cm

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 900 and a customer pays Rs. 630 for it. What is the discount percentage?
questions.solution:
Given,

Marked price (M.P.) of the article = Rs. 900

Selling price (S.P.) of the article = Rs. 630

Discount = M.P. – S.P. = 900 – 630 = Rs. 270

⇒ Discount % = (270/900) × 100 = 30%

∴ Discount % = 30%

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 45% more than its cost price. If a discount of 20% is given, then what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Discount is calculated on the marked price

Profit is calculated on cost price

Profit% = [(S.P – C.P)/C.P] × 100

Selling price = Marked price - Discount

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be Rs. 100

Marked price = 100 + 45% of 100 = Rs. 145

Discount of 20% on Marked price = 20% of 145 = Rs. 29

⇒ Selling price = 145 - 29 = Rs. 116

Profit% = [(116 - 100)/100] × 100

⇒ Profit% = 16%

∴ The profit percentage is 16%

questions.question: The average of 40 numbers is 50 and that of other 60 numbers is 70. What is the average of all the numbers?
questions.solution:
Average of 40 numbers = 50

Sum of 40 numbers = 50 × 40 = 2000

Average of other 60 numbers = 70

Sum of other 60 numbers = 70 × 60 = 4200

Sum of all numbers = 2000 + 4200 = 6200

∴ Average of all numbers = 6200/(40 + 60) = 6200/100 = 62

questions.question: If the cost price of 8 articles is equal to the selling price of 6 articles, then what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price (C.P.) of each article be Re. 1.

Selling price (S.P.) of 6 articles = C.P. of 8 articles = Rs. 8

C.P. of 6 articles = Rs. 6

Profit = S.P. – C.P. = 8 – 6 = Rs. 2

Profit % = (Profit/C.P.) × 100 = (2/6) × 100 = 33.33%

∴ Profit % = 33.33%

questions.question: An article is sold at 10% profit instead of 5% loss, the man gains Rs. 75 more. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of that article?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price (C.P.) of the article be Rs. x.

We know that,

S.P. = C.P. – Loss (or) S.P. = C.P. + Profit

Selling price (S.P.) of the article at 5% loss = x – (5% of x) = Rs. 0.95x

S.P. of the article at 10% profit = x + (10% of x) = Rs. 1.1x

Additional gain = Rs. 75

⇒ 1.1x – 0.95x = 75

⇒ x = 75/0.15 = Rs. 500

∴ C.P. of the article = Rs. 500

questions.question: When 30 is subtracted from 45% of a number, the result is 150. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be N.

45% of N = 0.45N

According to the question,

0.45N – 30 = 150

⇒ 0.45N = 180

⇒ N = 180/0.45 = 400

∴ The value of the number = 400

questions.question: If one-third of a number is 35, then what will be the 64% of that number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be N.

According to question,

N/3 = 35

⇒ N = 35 × 3 = 105

64% of the number = 64% of 105 = 0.64 × 105 = 67.2

∴ 64% of the number = 67.2

questions.question: A person goes from point A to B and comes back. His average speed for the whole journey is 30 km/hr. If his speed while going from A to B is 24 km/hr, then what will be the speed of the person (in km/hr) while coming back from B to A?
questions.solution:
We know that,

**If ‘x’ km/hr is the speed from A to B and ‘y’ km/hr is the speed from B to A then,**

**Average speed = 2xy/(x + y)**

⇒ 30 = (2 × 24 × y)/(24 + y)

⇒ 15(24 + y) = 24y

⇒ 9y = 24 × 15

⇒ y = 40 km/hr

∴ The speed of the person while coming back from B to A = 40 km/hr

questions.question: A person goes from point S to T and comes back. His average speed for the whole journey is 70 km/hr. If his speed while coming back from T to S is 80 km/hr, then what will be the speed of the person (in km/hr) while going from S to T?
questions.solution:
We know that,

If ‘x’ km/hr is the speed from A to B and ‘y’ km/hr is the speed from B to A then,

Average speed = 2xy/(x + y)

⇒ 70 = (2 × x × 80)/(x + 80)

⇒ 35(x + 80) = 80x

⇒ 45x = 35 × 80

⇒ x = 62.22 km/hr

∴ The speed of the person while coming back from S to T = 62.22 km/hr

questions.question: Equal principal is invested in schemes of compound interest and simple interest. The interest obtained in the compound interest and in the simple interest schemes after 2 years is Rs. 3520 and Rs. 3200 respectively. If the rate of interest is 20%, then what is the principal (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
We know the formula for simple interest-

SI = (P × T × R)/100

Where,

SI = Simple interest

P = Principal

R = Rate of interest

T = Time period

⇒ 3200 = (P × 2 × 20)/100

⇒ P = Rs. 8000

∴ The principal amount = Rs. 8000
